profile.tagline: Pin any Solana account layout to a versioned schema and catch breaking changes before mainnet.
profile.full_description: Slotmap is a developer toolchain for Solana that lets teams declare versioned account schemas for any Anchor program and automatically diff incoming program binaries against registered layouts before deployment. The CLI command `slotmap diff` fetches the live discriminator map from mainnet via RPC, compares it against the local IDL, and emits structured field-level breaking-change reports including affected borsh offsets, type mutations, and downstream CPI callers. An on-chain PDA registry stores published schema versions so external teams at protocols like Kamino or Meteora can subscribe to upstream layout changes and receive webhook or on-chain event alerts automatically. A CI/CD pre-deploy gate integrates directly into Anchor build pipelines and blocks deployment if breaking changes are detected against registered dependents. Slotmap targets the specific failure mode where cross-program account parsing silently corrupts data or panics at runtime when an upstream protocol upgrades its account struct.
profile.team_description: The team consists of Solana protocol engineers with hands-on experience building and auditing Anchor programs across DeFi integrations, including prior work on cross-program invocation tooling and on-chain indexing infrastructure. They have direct exposure to production incidents caused by upstream account layout changes at mid-size Solana protocols.

roadmap.goal: Ship a working CLI that diffs local Anchor IDL v2 against live on-chain IDL and outputs field-level breaking change reports.
deliverables: `slotmap diff` CLI command parsing borsh struct layouts and emitting structured JSON reports with field offsets, type changes, and discriminator mismatches
Anchor build hook integration that runs the diff automatically as a pre-deploy step and exits non-zero on breaking changes
Test suite covering 10 real mainnet programs including Drift, MarginFi, and Phoenix with known historical layout changes

roadmap.goal: Launch the on-chain PDA schema registry on mainnet and enable downstream teams to subscribe to upstream program schema changes.
deliverables: On-chain PDA registry program deployed to Solana mainnet allowing teams to publish and version account schemas with a `slotmap publish` CLI command
Subscriber registration system where external teams declare dependencies on upstream program schemas and receive webhook POST notifications on schema changes
GitHub Actions workflow template that polls the registry for upstream changes and fails CI if a subscribed dependency has an unacknowledged breaking change

roadmap.goal: Release a web-based discriminator map explorer and grow the registry to 50+ indexed Solana programs with active downstream subscribers.
deliverables: Visual diff UI showing borsh field offsets, byte sizes, and type changes across program versions with side-by-side schema comparison
Indexed snapshots of 50+ major Anchor programs including Kamino, Jito, Meteora, and Orca with historical schema version timelines
On-chain event emission from the registry program so downstream programs can read schema change signals directly inside smart contract logic via CPI

original_idea.tagline: Pin any Solana account layout to a versioned schema and catch breaking changes before mainnet.
original_idea.problem: Solana programs store state in raw byte arrays with no enforced schema — when a protocol upgrades its account layout (adding a field, reordering discriminators, changing borsh structs), downstream programs and indexers silently break with no warning. In 2026, as Solana composability deepens across Drift, MarginFi, Phoenix, and hundreds of Anchor programs, cross-program account parsing failures are one of the top causes of production incidents, yet there is no standard tooling to catch them before deployment.
original_idea.solution: Slotmap lets developers declare a versioned account schema for any Solana program — expressed as typed field definitions against borsh/zero-copy layouts — and automatically diffs any new program binary against the registered schema before deployment. It runs as a CLI plugin that integrates into Anchor build pipelines, fetches the live discriminator map from mainnet via RPC, compares it against the incoming IDL, and emits structured breaking-change reports with field-level diffs and affected CPI callers. Schemas are stored in an on-chain registry (a simple Program Derived Address store) so external teams can subscribe to upstream schema changes and get alerts automatically.
original_idea.target_user: Solana protocol developers and integration engineers at teams like Kamino, Jito, or Meteora who depend on parsing upstream program accounts in their own smart contracts or off-chain indexers and need to catch breaking layout changes before they cause silent data corruption or runtime panics.
original_idea.unique_insight: Solana's raw byte-packing model gives maximum performance but zero schema enforcement — the ecosystem has accepted this as a fact of life, but composability at scale makes it an acute reliability problem that a lightweight registry layer can solve without changing the runtime.
core_features: CLI command `slotmap diff` that compares a compiled Anchor IDL against the live on-chain IDL and emits field-level breaking change reports
On-chain PDA schema registry where teams publish versioned account layouts, queryable by any downstream program
Subscriber alert system: external teams register their dependency on an upstream program's schema and receive webhook or on-chain event notifications when it changes
CI/CD pre-deploy gate: Anchor build hook that blocks deployment if breaking changes are detected against registered downstream dependents
Discriminator map explorer: visual diff UI showing borsh field offsets, sizes, and type changes across program versions
original_idea.why_now: Solana's composability surface exploded in 2025-2026 with restaking vaults, liquidity layer protocols, and cross-program yield strategies — teams are now parsing 10-20 upstream program accounts in a single transaction, making any upstream layout change catastrophic. Anchor IDL v2 standardized enough of the schema surface that a diffing tool is now actually feasible to build without custom parsers for every protocol.
